A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the list H-coloured graph problem is NP-complete for every graph H that is not a union of complete graphs, a union of cliques, a union of complete bipartite graphs, a union or a disjoint union of cycles and paths, a union of stars and a disjoint union of stars and cycles.
the list H-colours problem is in P iff H is a clique, is NP-complete if H is an arbitrary graph, is L-complete if H is a tree and is NL-complete if H is the empty graph.
the list H-coloured graph problem is the most general and the simplest CSP that can be solved in linear time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the list homomorphism problem for graphs can be solved in polynomial time if and only if the problem of deciding the existence of an H-homomorphism can be solved in linear time.
the computational complexity of H-colouring is determined by the structure of H and the complexity of the set of its homomorphisms.
the list homomorphism problem for graphs is not just a special case of CSP, but a very special one: its complexity is determined by the algebraic properties of the graph.
